exposure: none: read only tools/audit/briefs/D3.md, COMMON.md, README.md, finding.schema.json at origin/main, plus production and test sources at the baseline. No docs/audit-*.md, no backlog.md, no round3/round4, no gh, no CHANGELOG or pull-request bodies. Findings D3-01..D3-08 are my own measurement; the recorded CI numbers I quote (run 35395283955, run 34658441338) come from tests/mutation_budgets.json in the baseline tree, not from GitHub.

findings.title: The mutation instrument's driver set is not the gate's: it never runs the differential golden step
findings.claim: tests/mutation_table.py drives its mutants with 8 of the 24 scripts tests/closures.json measures, and tests/env_drift.py --all -- the differential golden step CI runs under GOLDEN_MODE=drift -- is not one of them, so the survivor fraction recorded in tests/mutation_budgets.json (12 of 40, CI run 35395283955) is not the fraction this repository's PR gate would produce.
findings.mechanism: mutation_table.py's --scripts default is open_meteo, solar_alignment, plan_view, edge, entities, validate, optimality, features. A mutant is driven only by the intersection of that list with its file's measured closure, and the instrument records the survivors. tests/run.sh's drift mode instead selects the diff's closure from tests/closures.json and runs tests/env_drift.py --all at the baseline SHA, which is a check the instrument has no way to run. Every line the instrument records as surviving was therefore measured with the differential switched off.

findings.title: Out-of-range defrost duty is accepted and folded into the derate bucket, untested
findings.claim: Deleting the range guard at custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/defrost.py:314 lets a duty of 2.0 advance DefrostDerate.observe_duty's bucket and sample count, and no script in the gate -- including the differential -- fails on it.
findings.mechanism: observe_duty folds a MEASURED defrost duty into an exponential average. The guard `if not 0.0 <= duty <= 1.0: return` is the only thing that keeps a caller's out-of-range fraction out of self.duty and self.duty_counts; with it removed the bucket takes the bad sample, and duty_counts is what crosses DERATE_CONFIDENCE_SAMPLES to apply the derate.

findings.title: flow_setpoint's emitter-UA floor is untested: deleting it makes a zero-UA call raise
findings.claim: Replacing the `max(emitter_ua, 1e-6)` floor at custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/mixing_valve.py:109 with a bare `emitter_ua` turns flow_setpoint into a ZeroDivisionError for emitter_ua=0.0, and no script in the gate fails on it.
findings.mechanism: flow_setpoint returns target_temp + q_hold / max(emitter_ua, 1e-6). For emitter_ua = 0.0 the floor is the only thing standing between the call and a float division by zero; the probe measures the pristine call returning 5200021.0 (target 21.0 plus 5.2/1e-6) and the mutant raising.

findings.title: cheaper_hour_count's non-positive-COP guard is untested: deleting it divides by zero
findings.claim: Deleting the `if cop_f <= 0.0: continue` guard at custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/wood_fuel.py:147 makes cheaper_hour_count raise ZeroDivisionError on a zero COP instead of skipping the hour, and tests/wood_advisor.py -- the script whose whole purpose is this module -- does not fail on it.
findings.mechanism: cheaper_hour_count compares wood_sek against price / cop_f per hour. A record with a missing or zero COP folds to 0.0 through _force_float; the guard is what keeps that division out. With it gone the function raises on price/0.0, and on a negative COP it silently flips the comparison instead.

findings.title: StartCounter's already-running early return is untested: deleting it corrupts the start streak
findings.claim: Replacing `return False` with `pass` at custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/wear.py:72 stops the start counter resetting its streak when a sample agrees with the state it already holds, leaving the streak at 1 where the real code leaves it at 0, and no script fails on it.
findings.mechanism: StartCounter.observe confirms a start only after START_HYSTERESIS_SAMPLES consecutive disagreeing samples. The `if above == self.running: self._streak = 0; return False` arm is what makes the run of samples CONSECUTIVE: with the return deleted the streak carries across samples that agreed, so the next disagreement can be confirmed on fewer than the promised samples.

findings.title: SystemIdentification's plausible-bounds refusal is untested: an out-of-bounds fit is reported as completed
findings.claim: Deleting the plausible-bounds guard at custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/sysid.py:1276 stops identify() refusing a fit whose tau or ua lands outside (0.1, 200.0) x (0.01, 5.0), so a physically implausible fit is returned with completed=True and no reason, and no script fails on it.
findings.mechanism: identify() ends with `if not (0.1 <= tau <= 200.0) or not (0.01 <= ua <= 5.0): return SysIdResult(completed=False, reason='fitted parameters outside plausible bounds')`. That return is the only place the refusal exists; with it gone the result carries the implausible parameters as a successful identification, and downstream confidence-weighted consumers read it as evidence.

findings.title: Seven survivors include two mutants no check could ever fail on, which the reported survivor count does not separate
findings.claim: Of the 7 mutants that survived every gate script, 2 are equivalent mutants -- custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/pump_mode.py:242 (GUARD_OFF) and custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/__init__.py:337 (BOOLOP) -- so the survivor count the mutation instrument records mixes real gaps with lines that cannot be observed.
findings.mechanism: pump_mode.resolve's `if raw is None: return None` is redundant: _fold(None) is 'none', 'none' is in neither _ALIASES nor _STATUS_AMBIGUOUS, and no alias key folds to 'none', so _ALIASES.get('none') returns None either way (measured). __init__.py:337's `task is not None and hasattr(task, 'cancel')` differs from the OR form only for a non-None object without a cancel attribute, and hass.async_create_task returns an asyncio Task, which always has one. The instrument's GUARD_OFF and BOOLOP operators produce these, and nothing in mutation_table.py's recording distinguishes them from a genuine survivor.

findings.title: One gate script's measured closure is the whole package, and 53 script pairs cover >=0.80 the same production modules
findings.claim: tests/deployment_shape.py's measured closure contains all 74 production modules, and 53 of the 276 script pairs share at least 0.80 of their production-module closure, so the gate's diff-closure selection runs scripts that can only have been selected for coverage another selected script already has.
findings.mechanism: tests/closures.json records, per script, the production modules its run actually imported. tests/run.sh selects scripts by that closure, so a script whose closure is the whole package is selected by every diff that touches any production module. Where two scripts share nearly all of one another's closure, a diff that selects one selects the other for the same reason, and the two then spend their recorded seconds asserting over the same modules. This is a selection-cost claim, not a claim that the assertions themselves are duplicates: which mutants each script kills was NOT measured here (the pre-screen stops at the first killer), so the overlap of kill sets is left open.
